name: Wumeng Nasu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: sealang.net LTBA archive, full listing of 520 articles (searched for Nasu/Nosu/Nesu/Guizhou/Weining/Yi).
sources.note: No LTBA article treats Nasu/Nesu of Guizhou; nothing to read.

sources.citation: Gerner, Matthias. 2019. Highlights from three Language Families in Southwest China: Burmese-Lolo, Tai-Kadai, Miao. RFLR Monographs 3. Duisburg: Research Foundation Language and Religion. 150 pp. DOI 10.23772/9783947306916. Sec. 1.3.1 Phonology, pp. 4-6 (pdf pp. 25-27), Weining Neasu.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. First-hand sketch of Weining Neasu: eleven retroflex consonants (Table 1.3, p.5), vowel [ɤ] and [i-y] contrast, 'Wēiníng Neasu and Mílè Axi have four and five contrasting tones' (55/33/21/13, p.5-6), 'The syllable structure in most Yí languages is relatively simple C(C)V(V)T' (p.6). No occurrence of stress/accent/prominence/iambic/trochaic anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent full text layer).

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp. 'Nesu 呢苏 (Weining)' profile pp. 76-77; toneme table 4.18 p.107.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing. Second-hand inventory: 'The Nesu has 46 initials, 8 vowels (7 monophthongs and 1 diphthong), 4 tones (/55/, /33/, /21/, and /13/) (cf. YYFC 1983)'; lists Wusa, Wumeng, Mangbu, Shuixi, Panxian varieties. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the dissertation.
